Name: Pierre de Fermat
Major contribution: With Pascal, developed the early theory of probability through the problem of points (1654).

Name: John Graunt
Major contribution: Analysed the London Bills of Mortality and constructed the first known life table; pioneer of demography.
Remarks: One of the founders of political arithmetic

Name: Blaise Pascal
Major contribution: With Fermat, laid the foundations of the mathematical theory of probability.

Name: William Petty
Major contribution: Developed political arithmetic, the systematic use of quantitative data for questions of the state.

Name: Jacob Bernoulli
Major contribution: Proved the Law of Large Numbers in *Ars Conjectandi* (1713).

Name: Thomas Bayes
Major contribution: Formulated Bayes' theorem, the basis of Bayesian inference (published 1763).

Name: Gottfried Achenwall
Major contribution: Coined the term *Statistik* (1749) for the descriptive science of the state.

Name: Pierre-Simon Laplace
Major contribution: Developed the central limit theorem and Bayesian probability; applied probability to many sciences.

Name: Carl Friedrich Gauss
Major contribution: Developed the method of least squares and the normal (Gaussian) distribution of errors.

Name: Adolphe Quetelet
Major contribution: Applied statistics and the normal curve to social and human data; conceived the average man.

Name: Sir Francis Galton
Major contribution: Introduced regression and correlation; pioneered the study of variation and heredity.

Name: Francis Ysidro Edgeworth
Major contribution: Advanced statistical theory, correlation and methods of estimation.

Name: Karl Pearson
Major contribution: Developed the chi-square test, the correlation coefficient and the method of moments; founded *Biometrika* (1901) and the first university statistics department (1911).

Name: William Sealy Gosset (Student)
Major contribution: Developed the *t*-distribution and the *t*-test for small samples while working at Guinness (1908).
Remarks: Wrote under the pen name Student

Name: George W. Snedecor
Major contribution: Popularised the analysis of variance and named the *F*-statistic in Fisher's honour (1934).

Name: Sir Ronald Aylmer Fisher
Major contribution: Developed analysis of variance (ANOVA), the design of experiments, maximum likelihood and the *F*-distribution; author of *Statistical Methods for Research Workers* (1925).

Name: Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis
Major contribution: Introduced the Mahalanobis distance; pioneered large-scale sample surveys; founded the Indian Statistical Institute (1931).

Name: Jerzy Neyman
Major contribution: With E. S. Pearson, developed the theory of hypothesis testing; introduced confidence intervals and the theory of survey sampling.

Name: Egon Sharpe Pearson
Major contribution: With Neyman, formulated the Neyman--Pearson theory of hypothesis testing.

Name: Gertrude Mary Cox
Major contribution: Advanced the design of experiments; co-authored the classic *Experimental Designs* (1950) with Cochran.

Name: Frank Yates
Major contribution: Developed missing-plot techniques, experimental design and the analysis of factorial experiments at Rothamsted.

Name: Abraham Wald
Major contribution: Founded statistical decision theory and sequential analysis; identified survivorship bias.

Name: Calyampudi Radhakrishna Rao
Major contribution: Gave the Cramer--Rao bound and the Rao--Blackwell theorem; major contributions to estimation theory.
